sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Our older Mannheim data covers only a handful of garages and has a gap from mid-2024 to August 2026, so we show no trend; the figures below are for weekdays in August and September 2026. Covid's low was April 2020, when the garages we then measured were 24% occupied.

Mannheim has been testing how far it can take cars out of the Quadrate. A traffic trial from March 2022 closed Fressgasse and Kunststraße to through traffic at Paradeplatz and turned their short-stay street spaces into public space, while keeping every garage reachable from the ring road [0]. The trial ended in May 2023. The delivery zones, bike parking and restaurant terraces that replaced street parking were kept, and the council asked for a new concept to reduce traffic on both streets [2]. Residents' permits rose in steps to €127.50 a year by 2025 [3]. Since February 2026 street parking in the centre costs €4 an hour [4]. The Masterplan Mobilität 2035+, adopted in 2025, is a framework of more than 100 measures still needing individual approval [15]. The Bundesgartenschau of 2023 drew more than 2.2 million visitors [13], with drivers directed to park-and-ride at the Maimarkt [12].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The city's garage company, MPB, is using price to pull drivers off the street. During the 2022 trial the city already advertised cheap first half-hours in the central garages [1]. Since April 2026 its 13 central garages, almost 4,000 spaces, charge nothing for the first 30 minutes, €2 for the first hour and €1 an hour at night, half the street rate [5]. Our tariff data records the standard hourly rates, not these first-hour offers.

MPB has also been expanding and modernising. In 2024 it bought the 363-space Kaufhof garage in N7 [6], next to the department store that closed in 2020 [10]. The Galeria at Paradeplatz was saved from closure in 2024 [11]. The N2 garage, built in 1964–67, was listed as a monument in December 2024 [7]. Many MPB sites now take drivers by number plate rather than ticket, and MPB aims to convert them all [8]. The largest charging offer in a Quadrate garage in 2023 was twelve points, in a private garage [9].

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
MPB runs every garage we measure. They average 37–38% on weekdays and 31% at weekends; Mannheim's centre is used more in the working week than at weekends. Location matters less than in most cities, because the Quadrate are compact and every garage is close to the centre. The main-station garages are the busiest (P1 49%, P3 48%), though the large P5 garage there stands at 25%.

On the tariffs we hold, the cheaper garages were the fuller ones. D3 (€1.50 an hour) ran at 47%, while the €3 garages in the N blocks and at the Kunsthalle ran at 25–42%, a moderate link. How the April 2026 tariffs change this will show in the data over the coming months.
